key_insight: A human–AI discovery loop produced the five-parameter Generalized Boyd algorithm, overcoming degree-skipping in constructions of irreducible integer polynomials with small Mahler measure.
engineering_relevance: The work illustrates how AI-assisted solver development, distributed numerical search, and exact symbolic verification can jointly advance computational mathematics.
method: Prototype numerical and symbolic solvers through human–AI interaction.
Run parallel searches on distributed clusters.
Extract mathematical hypotheses and verify candidate polynomials exactly.
evidence_signal: Across all even degrees up to 2000, the approach constructs polynomials below Boyd’s limit point of approximately 1.255434, improves six published values, and holds 99.6% of best-known records.
watch_item: The reported evaluation is bounded at degree 2000, and the construction does not resolve Lehmer’s underlying lower-bound problem.
paper_title: Breaking the high-degree barrier in Lehmer's problem with a human-AI discovery loop
